title: Cold framing on an ext4 NVMe server reads at half the speed of dd
body:
sufr's measurements of `Framed::open` on a server with Dell enterprise NVMe under ext4 on LVM, reported from its session and read with libsail 0.4.3:

| input | warm | cold |
|---|---|---|
| 90.1 GB, 2.57 M records | 14.4 s, 6.2 GB/s | 60-61 s, 1.5 GB/s |
| 21.5 GB, 100 M records | 5.7 s | 16.2 s |
| 19.5 GB, 516 K records | 2.6 s | 13.0 s |
| hg38 without N, 3.1 GB, 455 records | 0.55 s | 2.13 s |

Cold means `posix_fadvise(DONTNEED)` on the file before each run. Plain `dd bs=8M` of the 90 GB file, cold, one run each, read at 2.96 GB/s with one stream and 3.4 to 3.6 GB/s with 4 to 32 streams. Framing warm runs at 6.2 GB/s, so the scan is not what holds the cold read to 1.5 GB/s. `Framed::map` took the same cold time as `Framed::open`. `read_ahead_kb` is 128 on every block device there.

`Framed::open` builds its index with `build_index`, which reads 64 KiB at a time (`index::CHUNK`).

On an AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D with a Samsung 990 PRO, the gap does not reproduce. A cold uncompressed 1 GiB file framed at about 7.4 GB/s, the drive's rated speed, and a plain read with `memchr::memmem` took the same time at 64 KiB, 1 MiB and 8 MiB per read. The harness is `tmp-claude/2026-11-19-fasta-gap/repro/src/floors.rs` in the sail checkout, variants `framed`, `rs64k`, `rs1m` and `rs8m`.

## Proposal

Run those four variants cold on the server before changing anything, together with a variant that calls `posix_fadvise(POSIX_FADV_SEQUENTIAL)` before reading. If larger reads or the hint close the gap to one `dd` stream, `build_index` and `Reader::fill` take the change.

## Open

- Whether the cause is the read size, the readahead window, or something about LVM on that server.
